Disconnected from 100.84.159.38 port 22
I have a memory note about exactly this. Let me read it.

---
name: ssh-agent-and-ai-dev-access
description: "SSH keys live on the 1Password agent socket, not $SSH_AUTH_SOCK; how to reach ai-dev directly"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 5c1c46ab-2eef-48c1-8ca4-d8036533b6c9
  modified: 2026-08-11T04:22:07.025Z
---

In Claude Code's shell, `$SSH_AUTH_SOCK` points at Apple's launchd agent, which
holds no keys — `ssh-add -l` there always says "The agent has no identities",
even when 1Password is unlocked. The real keys are on
`~/Library/Group Containers/2BUA8C4S2C.com.1password/t/agent.sock`, which
`~/.ssh/config` selects for `ssh` via `IdentityAgent`. Never use `ssh-add -l` as
an unlock/readiness check; test with `ansible <host> -m ping` or a real `ssh`.

When 1Password locks mid-run, ansible fails with `agent refused operation` then
`Too many authentication failures` and the host goes UNREACHABLE — long deploys
die silently partway through.

Direct SSH to ai-dev needs the user `michael` and the key pinned, or the agent
offers too many keys and the server disconnects:

```sh
ssh -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -i <file-containing-ai-dev-pubkey> michael@ai-dev
```

Related: [[project_infrastructure]]

The memory note explains this exactly. Two things are off in `mm@ai-dev`: the username should be `michael`, and the 1Password agent offers too many keys unless the identity is pinned. Let me check the current SSH config and agent state.

content.text:
Fixed. Two separate faults were stacked:

**1. Wrong username (the actual error)**
`mm@ai-dev` overrode the `User michael` in `~/.ssh/config`. `mm` has no authorized key there, so every key was rejected and the server cut the connection after 6 failures — that's the "Too many authentication failures".

**2. No key pinning**
The 1Password agent holds 6 keys and offers all of them, so even the right username was one failure away from the same disconnect. ai-dev accepts the `macbook` key (`SHA256:LVA3PVx...`).

Changes:
- `~/.ssh/ai-dev.pub` — exported the `macbook` pubkey from the agent
- `/Users/mm/dev/nix-config/home/ssh.nix` — added `IdentityFile ~/.ssh/ai-dev.pub` and `IdentitiesOnly yes` to the `ai-dev` block (the `~/.ssh/config` is a read-only home-manager symlink, so it had to be changed at source), then `darwin-rebuild switch`

Verified: `ssh ai-dev` now offers exactly one key and lands as `michael` on Linux x86_64.

**Side effect worth knowing:** `darwin-rebuild switch` ran `brew bundle`, which quit 1Password. The agent socket stayed on disk but refused connections, producing a misleading "Permission denied (publickey)" immediately after "Server accepts key". `open -a '1Password'` restored it. I recorded this in the memory note.

**Still failing, unrelated:**
```
herdr --remote ai-dev
error: nested herdr is disabled by default.
```
